1620.notes: Title, institution and building photo inspected; no substantive sensor content.

1621.notes: Two learning objectives inspected: sensor roles and working principles. Roadmap only; substantive content follows.
1621.exclusionReason: Learning-objective roadmap; all substantive targets covered on later pages.

1622.notes: All three bullets viewed. Sensors observe environment or internal state and deliver physical-condition information. The absolute claim that robots cannot operate autonomously without sensors needs a bounded interpretation: open-loop programmed behavior can exist, but adaptation to unobserved changes is unsupported.

1623.notes: Transduction and all six roles viewed: perception, closed-loop control, safety, learning, localization, manipulation. Sensors provide evidence, not an automatic guarantee of stability or safety.

1624.notes: Both columns and every example viewed. Proprioceptive: potentiometer, encoders, IMU, joint torque, current, tachometer. Exteroceptive: cameras, LiDAR, sonar, force/tactile, GPS/GNSS. Classification follows measured role; contact force and joint torque may be related but listed separately.

1625.notes: All definitions viewed: range endpoints; span=max-min; signed error=measured-true; resolution; accuracy; repeatability/precision; dead band; dead time; bandwidth Hz. Dead band wording no output is shorthand for no response/change, not necessarily zero signal. Distinguish bandwidth from sample/update rate and dead time from overall latency.

1626.notes: All five definitions viewed: latency, output-per-input sensitivity, direction-dependent hysteresis, linearity, random noise. Proportionality wording is a simplified linearity definition; an affine calibration may include offset. Distinguish bias, noise and hysteresis; sensitivity has output/input units.

1627.notes: Every bullet and rotary component photo viewed. Three terminal divider uses supply, ground and wiper; linear track and negligible loading are needed for voltage proportional to position. ADC reads voltage, not angle without calibration. All four applications preserved.

1628.notes: Pin table 5V/GND/A0; diagram labels wiper/resistive strip/pins. Exact code A0, potValue=0, Serial.begin(9600), analogRead then println then delay(200). 0–1023 codes for 0–5V default example, 10-bit 1024 levels; distinguish quantization step from endpoint interpolation. Delay gives approximate maximum update rate ignoring overhead, not guaranteed exact sampling.

1629.notes: Full still photo viewed. Arduino Mega, three wires and rotary shaft connected; Serial Monitor repeatedly displays 541 at 9600 baud. Still image supports one code readout and setup, not a complete calibration curve or demonstrated response over time.

1630.notes: Both diagrams inspected: optical transmitter/slotted disk/receiver; four concentric absolute tracks with sixteen binary labels 0000 through1111. Four-bit example is binary labeling, not automatically Gray code. Incremental pulses need reference for absolute position; single-turn absolute angle after power-up does not automatically preserve multi-turn history.

1631.notes: All bullets/table and UNO illustration viewed. A to2, B to3, supply5V and GND. Phase difference gives direction; pulse counts give relative steps. Both pins are interrupt capable but following code attaches only A rising edges. Illustration is UNO even though lecture examples often say Mega; pins2/3 usable on both, not proof all board pin maps identical.

1632.notes: All code pixels read: volatile long count=0; PPR=600; INPUT_PULLUP pins2/3; attach only pin2 RISING; 9600 baud; noInterrupts encloses floating division count/PPR; interrupts restored before printing; Serial.println((int)rotations); delay50; ISR readsB HIGH increments else decrements. Integer cast truncates toward zero and hides fractional turns. Interrupts alone do not guarantee no lost pulses, especially masked intervals.

1633.notes: Full still viewed. Mega connected to rotary encoder; serial lines all Rotations: 0 at9600baud. Printed zero does not prove raw count zero because source casts fractional signed turns to int; no dynamic rotation sequence shown.

1634.notes: All bullets and diagram rays viewed. IR LED sends light toward surface, photodiode receives reflection; intensity fed to comparator produces digital classification. Reflectivity/angle/ambient light affect signal as well as distance; digital threshold is not a calibrated range value. Three applications line-following, obstacle avoidance and edge detection.

1635.notes: TableVcc5V/GND/OUT8; module photo labels VCC/GND/OUT and adjustable potentiometer. Code INPUT pin8,9600baud,digitalRead,stateHIGH prints Obstacle Detected else No Obstacle;delay300. Explicit active-high convention in code/prose must not be universalized to all module hardware.
